content.title: Siemens Invests $165M in Carolinas Footprint to Support AI Data Center Demand
content.text: Siemens is expanding its US manufacturing footprint with a $165 million investment across North and South Carolina, targeting rising demand tied to AI-driven data center growth. Expanding AI Infrastructure Capacity The investment focuses on scaling production of low- and medium-voltage electrical equipment critical to powering data centers. The new and expanded facilities are designed to streamline production, assembly, and delivery timelines. These capabilities are expected to support faster deployment of infrastructure needed for hyperscale data centers and emerging AI factories. New Facilities in North Carolina In Raleigh and Wendell, Siemens is adding multiple sites, including two all-electric facilities aimed at reducing operational emissions. The Raleigh site will assemble prefabricated power distribution systems, which can shorten installation timelines for large-scale projects. Meanwhile, the Wendell expansion includes localized production of protection and automation devices, along with increased switchgear manufacturing. Together, Siemens expects these projects to add hundreds of jobs and strengthen regional supply chains for electrical components. South Carolina Manufacturing Growth In Spartanburg County, Siemens is opening a new facility dedicated to the production and distribution of lighting panels. Nearby Roebuck will see expanded busway manufacturing capacity, supported by additional fabrication lines and finishing capabilities. These upgrades are intended to address bottlenecks in electrical equipment supply, particularly as data center construction timelines continue to compress, according to the industrial automation company. Workforce and Long-Term Strategy Beyond physical infrastructure, Siemens is also investing in workforce development through training initiatives aimed at electrical careers. Programs are designed to build a pipeline of skilled labor to support both manufacturing operations and broader grid modernization efforts. The Carolinas investment builds on Siemens Energy’s earlier $1 billion US expansion of gas turbine and grid equipment production.
